title: UK DMO short conventional gilt auction — moved forward a day to Tuesday 10-27 so it clears before the Budget
source: EST: dmo.gov.uk/media/qpeksrc0/pr280826.pdf — the UK Debt Management Office's own press notice of 28 August 2026, 'Calendar of gilt auctions and planned programmatic gilt tenders in October to December 2026', fetched direct 2026-10-16 (HTTP 200, 193,999 bytes, text layer decoded locally). Its Table 1 lists 'Tuesday 27 October | 10.00am | size and further details announced Tuesday 20 October' (3:30pm column header), with the gilt left unnamed. The 27 October row's footnote is in the earlier consultation agenda dmo.gov.uk/media/5kek12uu/sa170826.pdf (17 August 2026, same fetch day): 'This auction was previously scheduled for Wednesday 28 October 2026. Due to the timing of the Budget on 28 October 2026 the auction has been moved to Tuesday 27 October 2026.' Date, 10:00 London close and 20 October announcement are the DMO's own; the stock (a short conventional gilt per the 17 August table) and size are NOT yet announced. Stays estimate: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the calendar's confirmed-prefix list has no slot for the DMO
notes: Proposed 2026-10-16 by the uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28 D-12 pulse (proposals/uk-gilt-auction-short-2026-10-27.from-uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28.json, read as input and now shadowed by this canonical file); researched 2026-10-16 (docs/research/events/uk-gilt-auction-short-2026-10-27.md). It is the last scheduled gilt-supply read before the Budget: the DMO moved it off 28 Oct to 27 Oct. Five short-gilt auctions since 2026-06-24 (DMO result notices, read direct) cover 3.07-3.47x with tails 0.1-0.4bp; the latest, 2026-10-14, took £5.0bn of the 4% Treasury Gilt 2030 at 3.41x, tail 0.2bp, lowest accepted yield 4.947% (4.789% on the 2026-09-10 launch of the same stock). IGLT.L moves 1.03x its normal absolute daily size on auction days (n=7), so this is a leading read on the parent's gilt-to-Treasury channel, not a trade. Attribution: 27 Oct also carries the US 5y auction, Consumer Confidence, Durable Goods and MSFT's print. No position is or will be sized to this: symbols [], low impact, estimate-dated.
